title: Robust embedding validation: interpretability probes & simulated-regression suite
creator: Avery Chen
description: Implement a comprehensive evaluation harness that exercises embedding accuracy, interpretability, and resilience to simulated regressions. Deliverables: (1) a stratified golden-corpus and tagging scheme for slices (lang, doc-type, query-intent, length), (2) an offline batch runner that computes retrieval/recall metrics and distributional drift scores, (3) interpretability probes that surface nearest-neighbor drift and token-level saliency for PR triage, and (4) a canary pipeline that runs lightweight checks on runtime-staged models before rollout. The harness should be extensible to reranking endpoints and report latency-sensitive signals so we can evaluate quality vs cost trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Golden corpus created with at least 12 stratified slices and documented labeling rules
Offline runner produces nightly reports: MRR@10, Recall@k, cosine distance drift, and a small-sample embedding interpretability dump
Regression simulator can apply five perturbation types (typos, paraphrase, anonymization, truncation, adversarial-synonym) and generate expected degradation baselines
Canary checks run in CI for model updates and flag >5% MRR drop vs pinned baseline for manual review
Dashboards added to Console with per-slice trends and automated alerts when drift score exceeds threshold
tasks: Define slice taxonomy and labeling guidelines (lang, vertical, long-tail doc types)
Curate golden corpus (10k queries, 50k docs) and store as immutable artifact
Implement offline runner (PySpark + infra job) and schedule nightly runs
Build perturbation engine and custody of synthetic variants
Design interpretability probes (nearest-neighbor deltas, prototype examples, token saliency co-occurrence)
Instrument telemetry (latency buckets, per-request token counts, cache-hit metadata)
Create Console dashboard and alerting rules; wire pager duty playbook
Write docs and on-call runbook; merge PR and create release note
telemetry_signals: Mean pairwise cosine distance (baseline vs candidate)
rollout_plan: Stage 0: run harness against nightly training checkpoints (no traffic)
Stage 1: CI gate - small-sample canary for each model PR (0.1% traffic simulation)
Stage 2: Canary on Dedicated - 1% real traffic for 24h with metric watch
Stage 3: Gradual rollout 10/30/100% with automated rollback on threshold breaches
notes: Trade-off: heavier perturbation battery improves coverage but increases nightly job cost; initial run set to medium battery (3 perturbation types) and expand on demand
Decision: use cosine-based distance for drift signal + auxiliary retrieval-based recall to capture semantic shifts
Follow-up: schedule a joint session with Solutions (Nina Patel) to validate slice taxonomy against real customer workloads
